description: Turn PDFs and EPUBs into audiobooks; subtitles or videos into dubbed videos (including translation), and more. For free. Pandrator uses local models, including voice-cloning (instant, RVC-enhanced, XTTS fine-tuning) and LLM processing. It aspires to be a user-friendly app with a GUI, an installer and all-in-one packages.
readme: # Pandrator **Make audiobooks, subtitles, voiceovers, sounds, and music in one workspace.** [Website](https://pandrator.liniewicz.eu/en) · [Tutorials with screenshots](https://pandrator.liniewicz.eu/en/tutorials) · [Voice samples](https://pandrator.liniewicz.eu/en/examples) · [Po polsku](https://pandrator.liniewicz.eu/pl) Turn a book into something you can listen to. Transcribe a recording, translate its subtitles, or give it a new voice. Add sound effects and background music. Pandrator brings the steps together in a browser interface, with room to review and refine the result as you go. Run speech and transcription models on your own computer, connect a cloud provider, or let your AI assistant help through MCP. Start with one workflow and add more when you need them. The [quick model guide](#choosing-your-first-speech-model) and [broader model and language matrix](#models-and-providers) help you choose a voice, language, and setup that suit your computer. Pandrator Manager installs the application and the engines you choose, then opens Pandrator in your browser. Older workspace data can still be imported. For the retired Qt desktop interface, use an [older release](https://github.com/lukaszliniewicz/Pandrator/releases). [![Download for Windows (.exe)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download_for_Windows-.exe-2563eb?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/lukaszliniewicz/Pandrator/releases/download/v.0.13.0/PandratorManager-0.9.30-windows-x86_64.exe) [![Download for Linux (.AppImage)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download_for_Linux-.AppImage-168572?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/lukaszliniewicz/Pandrator/releases/download/v.0.13.0/PandratorManager-0.9.30-x86_64.AppImage) Windows 10/11 and Linux desktop · x86-64 · Pandrator 0.13.0 / Manager 0.9.30 [All downloads & release notes](https://github.com/lukaszliniewicz/Pandrator/releases/latest) · [Installation help](docs/getting-started/installation.md) · [User guides](docs/README.md) ## New in 0.13.0 - **Refine audiobook pacing.** Keep short dialogue exchanges together, split long sentences more carefully, and adjust pauses when assembling the audio. - **Choose how EPUB content is read.** Set narration preferences for tables and illustration text, with better handling of footnotes and ruby readings. - **Edit captions without re-recording.** Display-only edits preserve the spoken text and recordings. New subtitle exports use your current display text; historical wording remains available when you need it. - **Keep related work together.** Organize projects in virtual folders and keep language versions under one project. - **Use more local speech options.** audio.cpp 0.9.2 adds French PocketTTS and Voxtral TTS. Kokoro offers optional Japanese support with a separate dictionary download. Voxtral's weights are licensed for noncommercial use. See the [0.13.0 release notes](https://github.com/lukaszliniewicz/Pandrator/releases/tag/v.0.13.0) and [detailed changes](docs/release-changes-0.13.0.md). ## Try your first workflow 1. **Download and run Pandrator Manager.** On Linux, make the AppImage executable first. Choose a parent folder; the Manager creates a `Pandrator` workspace inside it and opens the setup interface in your browser. 2. **Install Pandrator and the engine you need.** Start with one of the speech models below, or **CrispASR** for transcription. You can add other engines later. Docker, WSL, and a separate Python installation are not required. 3. **Make something small.** Choose **Generate an audiobook** and paste a short passage, or open **Quick Transcribe** to upload a clip or record your microphone. Listen, review, and save the result. Local models download separately on first setup; speed and memory requirements vary by engine and hardware. The Manager shows the available compute options. The Windows launcher is currently unsigned, so Windows may show an unknown publisher warning; the [installation guide](docs/getting-started/installation.md) explains this and the release checksums. ### Choosing your first speech model Choose a model that supports your text's language, then the voice controls and hardware you need. These are useful starting points: | Model | Recommended for | Documented speech languages | | --- | --- | --- | | [Kokoro 82M](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M) | Fast generation and modest computers. CPU-friendly, with ready-made voices. | English (American and British), Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, French, Hindi, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese | | [Qwen3 TTS](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS) through audio.cpp | Voice cloning with **Base**, or creating a voice from a description with **VoiceDesign**. A useful next step on modest hardware. | Mandarin Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian | | [BreezeTTS 2](https://huggingface.co/BreezeBlue/Breeze-TTS-2) through audio.cpp | Voice design, expressive generation, and cloning from reference recordings for non-commercial projects. | English, Mandarin Chinese | For AMD cards such as the **RX 480**, choose audio.cpp's **Vulkan** backend for Qwen. Use a model package that fits your available memory and try a short passage before a long book. CPU generation is also available; speed depends on the model, package, and computer. To reuse a designed voice, **describe it → audition candidates → save the chosen sample in the Voice Library → select it for narration**. With Qwen, use VoiceDesign to create the sample and Base to generate from that reference. Breeze can design a voice, save it for later generation, or clone a voice from a recording and its transcript. Record or upload your own clean reference samples when you already have the voice you want. Breeze's open weights and self-hosted outputs are for research and non-commercial use. For other languages or voice options, compare the [broader matrix](#models-and-providers), then filter the application's **Audio models** catalogue by language and capability. See [providers and voices](docs/guides/providers-and-voices.md) for setup and voice references. ## What would you like to make? | Start with… | Make… | Guide | | --- | --- | --- | | A book, document, or pasted text | Narrated audio or an M4B audiobook with chapters and cover art | [First audiobook](docs/getting-started/first-audiobook.md) | | An audio/video file or existing subtitles | Reviewed, corrected, or translated subtitles | [First subtitles](docs/getting-started/first-subtitles.md) | | A video or subtitle file | Synchronized speech and a dubbed video | [First voiceover](docs/getting-started/first-voiceover.md) | | A description or an audio clip | Reusable sound effects, music, and a mixed soundtrack | [Sounds and mixing](docs/reference/sounds-and-mixing.md) | | A recording and optional captions | Transcript-guided cuts, reviewed boundaries, and an edited video | [Recording editing with MCP](pandrator_mcp/guides/workflows.md#media-editing) | | A short clip or your microphone | A TXT, SRT, or JSON transcript without creating a session | [Quick Transcribe](docs/reference/quick-transcription.md) | ## Use the AI assistant you already have If you use **Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, or another MCP-capable host**, its model can do Pandrator's language work directly. You do not need to configure a separate LLM provider or API key in Pandrator for this route. In a **passive MCP workflow**, Pandrator prepares and tracks the work; the model in your existing conversation processes it and submits results through MCP. “Passive” describes Pandrator's role: it does not make the LLM calls itself. ```mermaid flowchart TD P["Pandrator prepares a batch"] --> A["Your agent corrects, translates, or optimizes"] A --> V["Pandrator validates and saves"] V -->|More batches| P V -->|Complete| R["Review and export, or generate speech"] ``` Use it to: - **Clean PDF/EPUB text** before audiobook preparation, with reviewable changes to document structure and extraction artifacts. - **Correct and translate subtitles**, keeping cue identities and shared terminology across batches. - **Optimize text for speech** before narration, while retaining the source wording as a separate artifact. - **Coordinate a whole workflow**: import a file, process the text, select a voice, generate speech, and return verified deliverables. After [connecting your MCP host](docs/operations/agent-connections.md), try a request such as: > Use Pandrator to correct this recording's English subtitles and translate > them into Polish. Use your own model through passive dispatch, keep a shared > glossary, and export both SRT files. Preserve uncertain wording for review. Pandrator tracks batches, validates submissions, and keeps completed work so an interrupted agent can resume. The agent must continue the tool loop; starting a passive run alone does not process it. Speech recognition and speech generation still use the engines you select in Pandrator. Your host's normal usage limits and costs apply. If its model runs in the cloud, the text it processes is sent there, even when Pandrator runs locally. See the [passive workflow guide](docs/guides/passive-dispatch.md), [end-to-end agent guide](docs/guides/agent-workflows.md), and the [reusable workflow skill](pandrator_mcp/skills/pandrator-workflows/SKILL.md). The skill adds workflow guidance; the MCP connection supplies the tools. See [skill installation](pandrator_mcp/README.md#optional-workflow-skill) to add it to your host. ## Features in more detail ### Audiobooks and narration - Import TXT, PDF, EPUB, DOCX, MOBI, or pasted text. MOBI conversion needs optional Calibre. - Prepare documents with extraction, OCR, chapter detection, text cleanup, and optional AI assistance. - Adjust pronunciation and speech text, generate in segments, compare takes, and regenerate selected passages. - Assign character voices and delivery directions. After changing the cast, regenerate the affected recordings and compare the saved Before and After audio versions. - Record or upload voice references and retain their transcripts. - Export WAV, MP3, Opus, FLAC, or M4B, with audiobook chapters, metadata, and cover art where the format supports them. - Export a video book with timed reading text, or save timed subtitles alongside the narration. ### Sounds and music - Generate sound effects or music from a description, or import your own clips. Available controls, including lyrics, depend on the selected model. - Save clips and alternate versions in a searchable library for reuse. - Place effects around spoken passages and mix background music with narration or voiceovers. Adjust timing, volume, trim, and fades while retaining the original speech recordings. See [sounds and mixing](docs/reference/sounds-and-mixing.md) and [choosing a sound or music model](docs/reference/sound-and-music-models.md). ### Subtitles, voiceovers, and recording edits - Transcribe audio/video with timestamps and optional speaker diarization. - Import SRT; WebVTT, ASS, and SSA uploads are also recognized, with SRT used as the working subtitle format. - Correct, translate, split, merge, and retime cues in a reviewable editor. Use manual edits, configured language providers, or passive MCP processing. - Generate synchronized speech and export media with selectable audio and subtitle tracks, including burned-in subtitles. - Plan recording cuts from a transcript, inspect and refine their boundaries, and render a reviewed edit while preserving the original media. ### Quick transcription and automation - Upload audio/video or record and preview your microphone, then copy or download TXT, SRT, or JSON without creating a permanent session. - Transcribe through HTTP or MCP: an approved-root file path or a small base64-encoded clip can be supplied through MCP. Larger files are streamed from the host rather than placed in the model's context. - Quick transcripts are temporary and expire one hour after completion; save the result you want to keep. - Use MCP for session workflows, live voice/model selection, reviewable plans, resumable work, and downloads verified by size and checksum. ## Models and providers This broader matrix covers the main speech models and providers. Language lists can differ between checkpoints, voices, and cloud models. “Listed” coverage means languages described in Pandrator's catalogue; a model can have broader upstream claims, and pronunciation quality still varies. Open **Audio models** for the full list and filter by the language and voice controls you need. Speech recognition and word alignment have separate language coverage. ### Local speech generation **audio.cpp is a local speech provider with several models to choose from, and the default for new workspaces.** Select the model packages you want to install in the Manager, then choose an installed model in **Generate audio** settings. You can switch models or add more later. Available families include: | audio.cpp model family | Voice options | Speech language coverage | | --- | --- | --- | | **Qwen3 TTS** | Base for cloning; CustomVoice for built-in speakers; VoiceDesign for a described voice. | Ten languages; see the quick guide above. Choose the appropriate Base, CustomVoice, or VoiceDesign package. | | **Fish Audio S2 Pro** | Expressive reference-voice cloning. | 83 languages reported by the model, including English, Mandarin Chinese, French, German, Spanish, Polish, and Dutch. | | **VoxCPM2** | Reference-voice cloning and described voices on supported packages. | 30 listed languages, including English, Mandarin Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Polish, and Dutch. | | **Chatterbox** | Reference-voice cloning; Turbo has its own voice and vocal-event controls. | 19 listed languages in the multilingual package; Turbo is English-only. | | **MagpieTTS** | Preset multilingual voices. | English, Arabic, Mandarin Chinese, French, German, Spanish, Hindi, Italian, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, and Vietnamese; choices depend on the voice. | | **OmniVoice** | Reference-voice cloning and described voices on supported packages. | Hundreds of languages; the main package lists 646 language entries. Related checkpoints can have narrower coverage. | | **PocketTTS** | Preset voices and reference-voice cloning. | Separate English, German, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish checkpoints; choose the one for your text. | | **FireRedTTS3 Base** | Experimental reference-voice cloning. | 24 listed languages, including English, Mandarin Chinese, Cantonese, Japanese, Korean, Polish, and Dutch. | | **BreezeTTS 2** | Voice design, generation from saved designs, and reference-voice cloning. | English and Mandarin Chinese; open weights and self-hosted outputs ar
